authoredFrom: the gates table in superpipeline apps/api/src/board/board-do.ts, the GateDecision union it resolves against, and charter decisions/2026-08-30-a-gate-closes-over-chat.md
purpose: A superpipeline approval gate crosses into a Matrix room and a human's answer crosses back. Three codebases must agree on the field names: the board that opens the gate, the Application Service that projects and resolves it, and the client that draws the buttons. A rename in any one of them is a gate that silently never resolves — which reads to the human as a button that does nothing.

howToRead.wireShape: The two directions are DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC. Outbound, a gate is a genuine custom Matrix event type `dev.superpipeline.gate.v1`, matching the three `dev.agentpod.*` types already shipping, because it needs a renderer: it is a question with buttons. Inbound, a decision is an ordinary `m.room.message` with `msgtype: "m.text"` carrying `suite_event_type` in content, because it needs no renderer: it is a sentence, and sending it as a message means it reads in every client with no registry entry and no risk of a reader seeing their own answer twice.
howToRead.versioning: Major version in the `suite_event_type` string (`.v1` → `.v2`) mints a new type and a new renderer. Minor version is `schema_version`, an integer inside content, bumped for additive changes only. A renderer written against v1 tolerates a higher schema_version by ignoring fields it does not know.
howToRead.accept: Payloads a consumer MUST handle. Field names here are the contract.
howToRead.reject: Payloads a consumer MUST refuse. These are the point of the corpus — a fixture of only-valid examples proves almost nothing, which is how the mem_/mbr_ drift survived in superpipeline for as long as both halves existed.
howToRead.stockClients: A stock client renders an unknown EVENT TYPE as nothing at all — not as fallback text. So a gate is accompanied by a companion prose m.room.message carrying the same question. That is the suite's existing convention, documented on supermessage's PermissionRequestRenderer: the event is sent beside an ordinary prose message so a client that never renders it is "exactly as able to answer as it was". superpipeline#34 assumed a custom event's own `body` would be shown by every client; that is true of an unknown MSGTYPE and not of an unknown EVENT TYPE.
howToRead.whichConsumer: `reject` binds the SENDER and the Application Service: payloads that must not be emitted and must not be acted on. It does NOT ask a renderer to refuse an unrecognised field — additive tolerance is required in the other direction, and a renderer refusing unknown keys would break the moment `schema_version` is bumped. A renderer's obligation for a reject case is narrower: offer no decision it cannot honestly resolve.
howToRead.gateIdPrefix: `gate_`, not `gat_`. superpipeline mints it with `idSchema('gate')` and its prefix registry maps gate → 'gate'. This corpus was first written with `gat_` copied from superpipeline#34's sketch and corrected when a test asserted the real prefix. NOTE: the `gate` entity is absent from id_grammar.json entirely — it is minted by superpipeline and, until this file, crossed no repo boundary. It belongs there now that it does.

optionIds.meaning: NOT free-form. superpipeline's resolveGate takes `GateDecision = 'approve' | 'request_changes' | 'reject'`, so an option id outside this set renders a button that is refused on resolution. superpipeline#34 proposed free-form ids mirroring a `select` signal's semantics; that is a good instinct and it is not what the endpoint does. Widening gates to arbitrary options is a `.v2`, not a field change.
optionIds.labelsAreFree: `label` is display text and carries no meaning. Per-board wording belongs there.
optionIds.v2: Applies to v1 only. gate.v2 (charter decisions/2026-11-07-gate-v2-is-the-decision-envelope.md) keeps no list: options come from the gate, each saying what it means, and superpipeline refuses an id the gate did not offer.

droppedDeliberately.run_id: superpipeline's gates gained a nullable `run_id` for evidence (superpipeline gate-run-id PR, SuperJackfruitLabs/superpipeline#145). The Matrix event still does not carry it: a room needs no run to ask or answer, and the event shape is unchanged.
droppedDeliberately.task_id: No such row exists in superpipeline's model. The pair is card and stage.
droppedDeliberately.expires_at: Gates do not expire. No column, no sweep, no alarm. An optional field nothing will ever set invites client code for an impossible case.
droppedDeliberately.tenant_id: superpipeline's internal isolation boundary. A room may have wider membership than a board, and no consumer needs it — the Application Service recorded which board a gate came from. (#34's sketch also wrote the prefix as `tn_`; the grammar pins `tnt_`.)

events.sender: the human's own Matrix session, so the actor is carried inherently. charter decisions/2026-08-14-approvals-cross-planes-as-events.md turns on this: a bridge substituting its own identity would void superpipeline's separation-of-duties check and every approval in the suite would attribute to one account.

notes.bothIdentifiers: `gate_id` AND the m.relates_to reference, deliberately. The reference is what a client uses to thread the answer under the question; `gate_id` is what the Application Service resolves on. Trusting only the reference would mean resolving a gate by chasing an event id an untrusted sender chose; trusting only `gate_id` would leave the answer visually unmoored. They MUST agree, and a consumer refuses when they do not.

notes.options: Each option is {id, label, meaning, needs_comment, delivery?}. NO list of valid ids: the carrier and the renderer carry what the gate offers, and superpipeline refuses an id the gate did not offer. A client draws by `meaning` (approve | reject | revise | choose | defer), never by id.
notes.olderBoards: A board that sends options as {id, label} only is still projected: meaning is derived (approve, approve_automatic, approve_manual → approve; reject → reject; request_changes → revise; anything else → defer) and needs_comment is true for request_changes only.
notes.subject: Present only on a gate bound to an approval subject: {id, digest, schema, revision, expires_at, preview, preview_complete}. preview blocks are {type: text, label?, text} | {type: field, label, value} | {type: link, label, url}; text and link url at most 4000 characters, labels and values at most 200, at most 20 blocks. preview_complete is false when anything was cut or dropped to fit; a client must not offer an approving option on an incomplete preview, or one whose blocks it cannot draw.
notes.body: For a subject-bound gate the body shows the preview — the exact post, fenced so markdown keeps every character — so a stock client sees what is being approved.

events.direction: outbound — an agent asks for a strict decision, or a board-dispatched harness permission
events.discriminator: `suite_event_type` in content, as for any question.v2. A consumer that finds the first question.v2 entry by suiteEventType reads the ordinary one; this entry adds `subject` and option `scope` / `requires`.

notes.subject: gate.v2's subject in snake_case: {id, digest, schema, revision, expires_at, preview, preview_complete}, re-bounded by the carrier as for a gate. schema is `salaam-operation/v1` (a strict decision: id = the offer's request id, digest = the decision digest) or `harness-permission/v1` (a board-dispatched harness permission). The digest is opaque: compared byte for byte, never computed.

events.direction: outbound — the board asks a person to choose one of several drafts
events.discriminator: `suite_event_type` in content, as for the entry without a variant; `subject` holds `variants` instead of a subject's identity.

notes.subject: { variants: [{ id, label, subject }] }, 1 to 3 variants, with NO top-level id or digest: a client that predates variants cannot read this gate.v2 as a subject and falls back to the v1 card, which never offers a subject approval. Each variant's subject is the usual snake_case envelope {id, digest, schema, revision, expires_at, preview, preview_complete}.
notes.bounds: Each variant's preview is bounded to an equal share of the whole-preview budget, floor(16000 / n) UTF-8 bytes of JSON-encoded strings, by the board and again by the Application Service, so one long draft never costs another its preview. A variant that was cut says preview_complete: false on its own; its siblings keep theirs.
notes.options: The usual four. The choice is the binding, not an option: a client offers an approving option for a variant only when that variant's preview is complete and drawable; request changes and reject act on the whole set and are always offered.
notes.malformed: More than 3 variants, an identity beside them, a variant without an id, label, id or digest, or two variants sharing an id or a subject: the Application Service carries no subject and offers only request_changes and reject.
notes.body: Every variant's label and bounded preview, fenced; a variant whose preview is incomplete is said to be chosen on the board.

accept.why: three variants, the third cut to its share by the board and so incomplete on its own

notes.quorum: { required, from, approvals: [{ principal_id, at, variant_id? }] }: required a whole number from 2 to 5; from "deciders" or "admins"; approvals the ones recorded so far, oldest first, each person at most once, at most 32. variant_id only on a variant gate. snake_case, from the board's camelCase quorum on gate.pending.
notes.absent: A gate that passes on one approval carries no quorum key at all, so its gate.v2 is byte-identical to before.
notes.malformed: A quorum that is not well formed is not carried: the Application Service omits the field rather than carry junk, and the gate then reads as one that passes on one approval, which superpipeline still judges.
notes.client: Hides approval from someone who has already approved and says how many more are needed. An older client shows the gate as before; superpipeline counts its answer once and refuses a second.
